text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski proposed creating an army modernisation fund which would double military outlays in the five years from 1998 and enhance the armed forces' compatibility with NATO standards.

- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural bank has contracted the listed Mostostal Warszawa and Exbud Kielce construction firms to adapt the former Kasparzak electronics office building to banking needs. The contract is worth 56.7 million zlotys.
- A 126 km section of the Wroclaw-Katowice motorway will be completed by autumn 2000, the Opole motorway contruction office's director Eugeniusz Mroz said.
- More than 40 percent of Poles attribute Poland's economic growth to market reforms while 25 percent have noticed no real changes, a survey by the CBOS polling institute said.
NOWA EUROPA

- Daewoo-FSO wants to sell 90,000 cars this year and to increase output to 155,000 cars in 1997. By 2001 Daewoo will invest $1.5 billion, while the arrest of the Polish operation's head Sok Chin-chol in Seoul will not affect plans in Poland, Daewoo Motor Company worldwide president Tae Gou Kim said.
- Secondary market traders in the National Investment Funds' privatisation certificates (PSU) will pay a 21 percent sales tax as of 1997, the finance ministry said.
- Bread prices in Krakow, southern Poland, have gone up by 50 percent since January this year.
- A cut in tax rates will strongly improve Poland's economic climate, the Poznan-based Wielkopolski Klub Kapitalu employers' group wrote to Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko.
- Foreign investments in Poland may reach $22 billion by 2000, the Polish Chamber of Commerce (KIG) and the Gdansk University Economics Department researchers said.
- Zabrze based coke combine KK Zabrze and the German VST Duisburg, controlled by Ruhrkohle, have formed a Carbopol joint venture, with founding capital of 16 million zlotys.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The US Cargill food processor has opened a glucose plant, at a cost of $35 million in Kobierzyce, Wroclaw province.
- Food prices in October 10 to 20 were 1.2 percent higher than in the same period last month, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- In the first nine month of 1996 Polish distilleries made 163,000 hectolitres of quality vodka, a 29.1 percent decrease compared with the same period last year, GUS said.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and a banking consortium headed by Austria's Creditanstalt Bankverein will provide the Golub Raczkiewicz Epstein Partnership with a $56.7 million credit to finance the Warsaw Financial Centre's construction in central Warsaw.
- The Czech CZKD tram maker will not deliver five trams this year in time to meet a contract with Poznan city authorities. Poznan is likely to cancel the 34.78 million zloty contract.
PARKIET

- The brokerage house of the Bank Ochrony Srodowiska environmental protection bank will start offering primary market securities and portfolio management following permission from the Polish Securities Commission (KPW).
- The Szczecin province prosecutor, on a motion by the KPW, in August began to investigate alleged forgery of financial data by the former management of listed construction firm Espebepe.
- Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy and the Institute for International Research (IIR) have organised a conference on Poland's capital market development now under way in London.
